requirements.businessContext: Backups & Restore covers the snapshot lifecycle for a league: an on-demand .zip download of current state, persisted JSON snapshots in the `backups` table (manual, gw1-lock, auction-complete triggers), per-format restore endpoints (TVT, triple-crown, auction) that wipe-then-reinsert fixtures or auction state from a parsed .zip or stored snapshot, and the idempotent auto-snapshot helper invoked from session-completion and the cron's per-GW pipeline. Restore is destructive and operates per-format with strict cross-league + cross-format guards on the multipart upload path; saved-snapshot path enforces league ownership via the SELECT's WHERE clause.

userStories.soThat: I can inspect or re-import an older state via the per-format import blocks

userStories.iWant: to delete an unwanted backup row
userStories.soThat: I can prune snapshots that are no longer relevant

userStories.soThat: I can recover from a corrupted fixture state without rebuilding manually

userStories.iWant: to restore PL fixtures from an uploaded backup .zip or stored snapshot

businessRules.rule: All backup/restore endpoints require an authorized league via `getAuthorizedLeagueId` (`x-session-type`, `x-session-id`, `x-league-id` headers); on failure return 403 Forbidden.
Active-league enforcement: admins (non-superadmin) only get a leagueId when the league `isActive=true`; otherwise authorization returns null → 403.
GET /backup returns a .zip with Content-Type `application/zip`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="backup-<slug>-<YYYYMMDD-HHmm>.zip"`, and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
GET /backup returns 404 when the league row does not exist (after the auth check passes).
The .zip always contains `meta.json` (leagueId, slug, name, format, season, generatedAt, backupVersion=1) so restore endpoints can validate identity.
`teams.xlsx` and `captains.xlsx` are emitted only when `league.format !== "auction"` (auction has its own onboarding); `chips.xlsx` is emitted only when `league.format === "tvt"`.
Auction sheets (`auction_teams_state.xlsx`, `auction_squads.xlsx`, `auction_clubs.xlsx`) are emitted only when `league.format === "auction"`.

Auction event-history sheets (trades, penalty_redemptions, slot_unlocks, wishlists, notifications, sessions, bids, bid_logs) are auction-only and each sheet is only included in the .zip when its row array is non-empty.
Backup fixtures include PL fixtures only; playoff fixtures (`isPlayoff=true`) are excluded because they're regenerated by the advance flow.
Team rows in backup carry the placeholder password `RESET_REQUIRED` (bcrypt hashes are not reversible); admin must reset passwords after a teams-restore.
Ghost teams (`isGhost=true`) are excluded from all backup row arrays (teams, captains, chips, auction state).
Captain matrix has one row per (team, player); column `n` (1..38) is "C" when that player was captain in GW n, else "".

Chip matrix has one row per team; cell value follows the import-chips alphabet: "W"/"D"/"C"/"SL"/"CB"/"UD" for valid, suffix "W" for wasted, "C:<opponentLoginId>" for Challenge Chips with an opponent.
Auction sessions sheet includes only sessions whose status is "completed" or "cancelled"; active/pending sessions are intentionally excluded so admin reschedules after restore.
Penalty redemptions sheet includes only rows with `redeemedAt IS NOT NULL`; pending penalties live on the active team's `penaltySlots` and aren't snapshotted again.
POST /backups inserts a row with `trigger="manual"`, generated id, current timestamp, and JSON-serialised non-null payloads; returns `{ success:true, id, trigger, createdAt, counts:{...} }`.
POST /backups always writes `fixturesJson` (column is `.notNull()`); other format-specific JSON columns are null when the corresponding format-gated row array is null/empty.

GET /backups returns `{ backups: [{ id, trigger, createdAt, includes:{ teams, fixtures, captains, chips, auctionTeamsState, auctionSquads, auctionClubs, gameweeks } }] }` ordered by `createdAt DESC`; JSON blobs are NOT included to keep the list response lean.

GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/backups returns includes.fixtures structurally always true (the fixturesJson column is NOT NULL by schema). The flag is kept for API stability but documented as non-distinguishing. The other includes.* flags reflect actual NULL vs populated state on their underlying nullable columns.

GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/backups returns an includes map with flags for all 16 *Json columns in the backups table — including the migration-0012 auction event-history columns (auctionTrades, auctionPenaltyRedemptions, auctionSlotUnlocks, auctionWishlists, auctionNotifications, auctionSessions, auctionBids, auctionBidLogs). Pre-migration snapshots show the new flags as false; post-migration auction snapshots populate them.
GET /backups/[backupId] returns 404 when the (backupId, leagueId) pair does not match a row — cross-league lookup is blocked by the WHERE clause.
GET /backups/[backupId] also returns 404 if the league row itself is missing (after backup row resolves).
GET /backups/[backupId] re-hydrates stored JSON into the BackupRows shape and rebuilds the .zip live, so later formatting changes naturally apply to old snapshots without data migration.

GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/backups/[backupId] synthesises BackupMeta from the current leagues row PLUS an inferredOriginalFormat field derived from which JSON columns are populated in the backup row. When inferredOriginalFormat differs from format, the snapshot was taken before a format change and restore tooling MUST refuse or warn. The BackupMeta type now has an optional inferredOriginalFormat field for downstream consumers.
Downloaded snapshot filename is `backup-<slug>-<trigger>-<YYYYMMDD-HHmm>.zip` where HHmm is derived from the row's `createdAt`.

DELETE /api/admin/[leagueId]/backups/[backupId] authorises via `getAuthorizedLeagueId` (403 on failure), verifies the row belongs to the league via `and(eq(backups.id, backupId), eq(backups.leagueId, leagueId))` (404 "Backup not found" on miss / cross-league lookup), then runs the same-filtered `db.delete(backups)` and returns 200 `{ success: true }`. `backups` is a leaf table so the delete cascades to nothing.

Both restore-tvt and restore-triple-crown enforce a cross-format guard on BOTH the multipart-upload branch AND the saved-snapshot ({backupId}) branch. For the saved-snapshot path the format is inferred from which JSON columns are populated in the backups row (loadRestoreSnapshot — see DEF-BACKUP-008's inferredOriginalFormat heuristic). Cross-format restores return HTTP 400 before any destructive operation runs.
POST /restore-triple-crown rejects with 400 when `league.format !== "triple-crown"`.
POST /restore-auction rejects with 400 when `league.format !== "auction"`.

Restore endpoints accept either `multipart/form-data` with a `file` Blob or JSON `{ backupId: string }`; missing/invalid input returns 400 with the helpful message `"Provide either a multipart `file` upload or JSON `{ backupId }`"`.
Multipart restore path rejects with 400 if the uploaded .zip is missing `meta.json` ("please re-export from this league via Download Backup").
Multipart restore path rejects with 400 if `meta.leagueId` is present and does not equal the target league (cross-league restore blocked before any destructive op).
Multipart restore path rejects with 400 if `meta.format` is present and does not equal the target league's format.

Saved-snapshot restore path (`{ backupId }`) blocks cross-league restore via the SELECT's `eq(backups.id, backupId) AND eq(backups.leagueId, leagueId)` clause; mismatched id+league pair returns 404 "Snapshot not found for this league"/"Backup not found".

Saved-snapshot restore path for TVT/triple-crown does NOT check the backup's original format — `loadRestoreSnapshot` synthesises `meta: { leagueId: row.leagueId }` only (no `format`), so a triple-crown snapshot restored via /restore-tvt skips the format guard. // CODE-CONFIRMED: may be a defect — format guard only fires on multipart path.

`restoreFixtures` refuses to wipe when `payload.fixtures` is missing or has length 0 — it throws a `RestoreGuardError` before any DB read or delete. Both `/restore-tvt` and `/restore-triple-crown` route handlers catch `RestoreGuardError` and return 400 with the guardrail message; league fixtures + cascaded results are provably untouched on the empty-payload path.
Fixture wipe cascades to results via `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `results.fixture_id`; admins lose recorded results unless the new fixtures regenerate them.
Fixture row resolution is case-insensitive on `teamLoginId`; rows whose home or away login isn't found are skipped and a warning is added (not a 4xx).
Fixture row with `Gameweek` outside [1, 38] or non-numeric is skipped with warning `Row N: invalid gameweek ...`.

If a backup references a GW number that has no row in the target league, restore auto-creates the gameweek with a placeholder deadline (now + 7*gw days at 11:00) and `isPlayoffs = gwNumber >= league.playoffStartGw`.
Restore-tvt preserves teams (no wipe of accounts/passwords) and defers captains + chips restore — non-empty arrays add warnings instructing the admin to use the legacy import-* blocks.
Restore-tvt success response: `{ success:true, fixturesInserted, warnings:[], message:"Restored N fixture(s). Captains + chips restore is a tracked follow-up..." }`.

Restore-triple-crown reuses `restoreFixtures` from restore-tvt; cup fixtures + UCL/UEL knockouts are NOT in the backup payload today (tracked follow-up — see DEF-TC-003). Only PL fixtures are restored.
Restore-tvt leaves stale `playoff_ties` rows after the fixtures wipe — cross-module defect tracked as DEF-PLAYOFF-003 in module 08; not re-logged here.

Restore-auction validates every referenced teamId (teamsState, squads, clubs, trades [proposer+target], penaltyRedemptions, slotUnlocks, wishlists, notifications, bids [nominator+highBidder], bidLogs) against the league's current teams; orphan ids return 400 listing up to 3 + count.

Restore-auction wipes auction state in strict order (bid logs → bids → sessions → ownership → club ownership → team penalties → auction scores → trade proposals → slot unlocks → wishlists → notifications), then resets per-team economy to defaults (`purse=initialBudget`, totalSpent/totalRefunds/totalIncome/penaltySlots = 0).
Restore-auction does NOT restore `auctionScores`; admin must reprocess each GW after restore so the scorer regenerates them from the rebuilt ownership state.
Restore-auction restores per-team economy from the snapshot — Purse, Total Spent, Total Income, Total Refunds, Penalty Slots, Bonus Slots (defaults to 0 when the older backup omits the column).

Restore-auction inserts event-history in FK order: sessions → bids (orphans dropped if sessionId not restored) → bidLogs (orphans dropped if bidId not restored) → penalty redemptions (`sessionId` set to null when its session wasn't restored — schema FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`) → slot unlocks → trades → wishlists → notifications.

Restore-auction is NOT transactional — if an insert fails mid-write, the wipe has already happened and league state is partially modified; response is 500 `"Restore failed mid-write — league state may be partially modified"`. // CODE-CONFIRMED: may be a defect — destructive without rollback.

Restore-auction success response: `{ success:true, restored:{ squads, clubs, teamsState, sessions, bids, bidLogs, penaltyRedemptions, slotUnlocks, trades, wishlists, notifications }, next:"Admin should reprocess each GW..." }`.
`writeAutoSnapshot(leagueId, trigger)` is idempotent on the (leagueId, trigger) pair — if a row already exists for that pair, the function no-ops (returns without inserting).

`writeAuctionCompleteSnapshot(sessionId)` derives the trigger string from session type/cycleNumber: `initial → "auction-initial-c0"`, `club-auction → "auction-club-c0"`, `mini-auction → "auction-mini-c<cycleNumber>"`. The schema-comment label "auction-complete" is a category, not a literal trigger value.
Session-completion paths that call `writeAuctionCompleteSnapshot` swallow errors with `.catch((e) => console.error(...))` — a snapshot failure never blocks the auction state transition.

backups.trigger stores one of: 'manual' (admin-clicked), 'gw<N>-auto' (cron pre-processing snapshot, idempotent per gameweek), 'auction-initial-c0', 'auction-club-c0', or 'auction-mini-c<N>' (auction-completion snapshots, idempotent per cycle). Many 'manual' rows per league are allowed; the cron and auction triggers are idempotent.
Backup row cascade-deletes when the parent league is deleted (`leagues.id` FK with `onDelete: "cascade"`).
All restore + backup-download endpoints set `export const maxDuration = 60` to allow long-running zip generation.
Malformed `meta.json` inside the .zip is treated as missing (caught silently in JSON.parse) so the route surfaces the friendly "missing meta.json" error instead of a parse stack trace.

defects.title: restoreFixtures wipes existing fixtures even when payload.fixtures is empty
defects.description: src/lib/backup/restore-tvt.ts:128-132 unconditionally deletes all fixtures for the league before the re-insert loop. If the uploaded zip's fixtures.xlsx is empty (or the saved snapshot's fixturesJson is `"[]"`), the loop inserts 0 rows but the wipe has already run — taking results with it via cascade. Admin sees `{ success:true, fixturesInserted:0 }` and no warning.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Refuse to wipe when payload.fixtures.length === 0 (return 400 with a guardrail message), OR run the entire restore inside a transaction so an empty insert rolls back the wipe.
defects.actualBehaviour: Fixtures table for the league is silently nuked. Cascade also clears `results`. The success response does not warn the admin.
defects.notes:
Quick fix: `if (payload.fixtures.length === 0) return { inserted: 0, warnings: ["Refusing to restore: payload has 0 fixtures — wipe aborted."] };` before the delete call. Better: wrap the whole restore in a drizzle transaction. Risk: data loss — most common when admin uploads a malformed zip or hits restore on a fresh league with no fixtures.
[DEV] Self-verified: tsc passes for touched files (pre-existing failures only in unrelated tests/league-types/tvt-*.spec.ts), manual diff review clean. The guard fires BEFORE any DB read or delete, so the league state is provably untouched on the empty-payload path. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases.

Expected behaviour now: POST /restore-tvt (and /restore-triple-crown) with a payload whose fixtures array is empty returns 400 with the message `"Refusing to restore: backup payload contains 0 fixtures — wipe aborted to prevent silent data loss. Re-upload a backup with a non-empty fixtures sheet."` and the league's fixtures + results tables are untouched. Cover both code paths: (a) multipart upload of a zip whose fixtures.xlsx is empty, (b) JSON {backupId} where the stored backups.fixturesJson is `"[]"`. Also re-confirm the happy path TC-BACKUP-031 (positive restore with non-empty fixtures) still works.

Both route handlers (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/restore-tvt/route.ts:95-97 and src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/restore-triple-crown/route.ts:84-86) now catch `RestoreGuardError` and return 400 with the error message instead of a 500. defects.title: restore-auction is non-transactional — partial state on mid-write failure
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/restore-auction/route.ts:356-573 runs sequential db.delete + db.insert calls outside any transaction. If any insert throws (FK violation, NOT NULL on a malformed backup row, transient DB error), the prior wipes (bids, sessions, ownership, club ownership, team penalties, auction scores, trade proposals, slot unlocks, wishlists, notifications, per-team economy reset) have already committed. The route returns 500 with the message acknowledging "league state may be partially modified", but provides no recovery path.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Wrap the entire wipe + restore inside `db.transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` so any error rolls back the whole operation atomically. The admin should see either a fully restored league or an unchanged one.
defects.actualBehaviour: Partial restore leaves the auction league in an unusable state: ownership wiped + economy reset but bids/sessions not yet inserted. Admin has no automated rollback; manual DB intervention required.
defects.notes:
Drizzle on Turso supports `db.transaction` for serial writes. Risk: HIGH — this is the most destructive route in the app (12+ tables wiped). Failure during restore means an unrecoverable league for admins without DB access. Recommend transactional wrap before any GA usage.
[DEV] Self-verified: tsc passes for the touched file (pre-existing failures only in unrelated tests/league-types/tvt-*.spec.ts), manual diff review clean — every write in the wipe + restore phase now uses `tx`, no `db.delete/insert/update` remain inside the transaction scope. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases.
[QA] Re-run TC-BACKUP-047 against the fix. Inject a forced failure (e.g. malformed AuctionSessionRow, FK violation on bids->sessions) mid-restore and confirm: (a) response is 500 with the new message 'Restore failed — transaction rolled back, league state unchanged'; (b) every wipe-phase table (auction_bids, auction_sessions, auction_ownership, auction_club_ownership, team_penalties, auction_scores, trade_proposals, team_slot_unlocks, auction_wishlists, notifications) and the teams.purse/totalSpent/totalIncome/totalRefunds/penaltySlots fields are unchanged from pre-restore state.
[QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-25 — TC-BACKUP-047 inverted; transactional restore confirmed.
defects.resolution: Wrapped the entire wipe + restore block in src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/restore-auction/route.ts:356-563 with `await db.transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` and replaced every `db.delete/insert/update/select` inside with `tx.*`. Reads outside the wipe (league lookup, team validation, stored-backup fetch) remain on `db` since they are read-only and must complete before any destructive op. The pre-existing try/catch now reports 'Restore failed — transaction rolled back, league state unchanged' since libsql rolls back the txn on any thrown error.
